skill.name: delphi
skill.description: Coordinates multiple parallel oracle agents with the same prompt, saves their reports, and synthesizes divergent findings into one answer.
skill.summary: Runs parallel Delphi-style investigations and synthesizes independent findings.
skill.author: Cygnusfear

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline paths, and platform Task examples. One real shell command creates an output directory from a user-derived topic without sanitization guidance. I also found semantic risks from unbounded parallel subagent fan-out and persistent full reasoning exports; no prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.issue: Shell directory creation uses a user-derived topic.
remediation.suggestion: Normalize the topic to a safe slug and create directories through filesystem APIs. If a shell is required, quote arguments strictly.

remediation.issue: Oracle count has no explicit upper bound.
remediation.suggestion: Set a hard maximum, such as five oracles, and require explicit confirmation for any higher count.

remediation.issue: Reports request complete reasoning and all relevant context.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for concise rationale, evidence, and caveats instead of complete chain of thought. Redact secrets before writing reports.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded Parallel Subagent Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill accepts any user-specified oracle count and then dispatches all oracles simultaneously. A large count can cause excessive cost, latency, and resource use.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 24-26 allow user-selected counts without a maximum, and lines 47-68 require simultaneous dispatch. The risk is resource abuse rather than malware.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Reasoning and Context Persistence
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells oracles to include all relevant context and export full thinking, entire elaborated thinking, and complete chain of reasoning to local files. This can persist sensitive user data and internal reasoning without redaction guidance.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines directly require all relevant context and complete reasoning exports. The risk is clear, though storage is local rather than external.

content.value_statement: Complex questions often benefit from independent investigation paths. Delphi runs multiple identical oracle prompts and synthesizes their reports into one clear answer.
actual_capabilities: Determines oracle count from the user request or defaults to at least three oracles.
Builds one shared prompt with the question, context, success criteria, and export instructions.
Instructs multiple general-purpose oracle tasks to investigate independently.
Saves oracle reports under the .oracle topic folder with numbered files.
Synthesizes convergent, divergent, and unique findings into a final document.
Presents key findings and offers deeper review of individual oracle reports.
limitations: Requires an environment that supports parallel Task or subagent calls.
Creates local .oracle files, so sensitive topics need careful handling.
More oracles increase token usage, runtime, and cost.
Results depend on available files, documentation, web access, and tool permissions.

use_cases.title: Investigate Production Incidents
use_cases.description: Run independent investigations into unclear failures and compare root-cause evidence before choosing a fix.

use_cases.title: Compare Architecture Options
use_cases.description: Explore tradeoffs from several independent paths before selecting a durable technical direction.

use_cases.title: Explore Research Questions
use_cases.description: Gather multiple perspectives on a broad question and merge the strongest evidence into a synthesis.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Investigation
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when the question is broad but low risk.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use delphi to investigate this question: [question]. Use three oracles and synthesize the strongest shared findings.

prompt_templates.title: Debug an Unclear Failure
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when a system problem has several possible causes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Ask delphi to analyze why [system] is failing. Include this context: [details]. Use four oracles and compare divergent root causes.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate an Architecture Decision
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when the answer requires tradeoff analysis.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use delphi to evaluate [architecture choice]. Include constraints, success criteria, and known risks. Synthesize recommendations with confidence levels.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Deep Multi-Oracle Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for complex investigations that need broad coverage.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a five-oracle Delphi investigation on [complex issue]. Require evidence, caveats, divergent interpretations, and a final action plan.

output_examples.input: Use delphi to investigate why checkout latency increased after the last release.
output: A synthesis names the most likely latency sources and separates confirmed evidence from hypotheses.
It highlights where oracles agreed, where they disagreed, and which logs or changes need follow-up.

output_examples.input: Ask delphi whether we should split the billing service into smaller services.
output: The final report compares reliability, team ownership, deployment risk, and migration cost.
It recommends a path and lists open questions that need measurement before implementation.

output_examples.input: Use delphi to research options for reducing support ticket volume.
output: The synthesis groups repeated findings across oracles and identifies unique ideas worth testing.
It ends with prioritized actions, expected impact, and confidence notes.

best_practices: Give the core question, relevant context, and success criteria before launching oracles.
Use neutral phrasing so every oracle starts from the same assumptions.
Review the synthesis and inspect individual reports when findings conflict.
anti_patterns: Do not use Delphi for simple factual questions that one focused search can answer.
Do not store secrets, credentials, or private customer data in oracle reports.
Do not specialize each oracle unless the user explicitly requests different roles.

faq.question: What does Delphi do?
faq.answer: It sends the same question to multiple oracle agents, then synthesizes their independent findings.

faq.question: Why use identical prompts?
faq.answer: Identical prompts reduce steering bias and let different investigation paths emerge naturally.

faq.question: How many oracles should I use?
faq.answer: Use three for most questions. Use four or five when the problem is complex and worth the extra cost.

faq.question: Where are results saved?
faq.answer: The skill saves oracle reports and the final synthesis in a local .oracle topic folder.

faq.question: Can it help with debugging?
faq.answer: Yes. It is useful when failures have unclear causes and several investigation paths are plausible.

faq.question: What should I avoid sharing?
faq.answer: Avoid secrets, credentials, regulated data, and private customer details unless local storage is approved.
